statement: For the constant deterministic edge law t_e=c>=0 on nearest-neighbor Z^2, the horizontal doubly infinite path is a bigeodesic.
assumptions: all edge weights equal finite c>=0
source: w391/CLAIMS.jsonl P0117-w391-C01; independently checked against the graph distance
proof_or_counterexample: Every path from (i,0) to (j,0) uses at least |j-i| edges; its weight is at least c|j-i|, attained by the horizontal segment. At c=0 every path ties and the path remains geodesic.
remaining_gap: Only refutes an extension permitting constant laws; does not address the target's nonatomic law.

statement: For 0<=l<h and integer w>=0, a slab with all m(2w+1) horizontal edges inside a width-w strip at least h and the top-row bypass and two boundary connectors at most l forbids an ambient geodesic confined to the strip from crossing m columns, provided m(h-l)>(4w+2)l.
assumptions: endpoints on the two slab boundary columns
proof_or_counterexample: A crossing meets each of m distinct vertical cuts, costing at least mh. From either endpoint height to row y0+w+1 costs at most 2w+1 edges per connector, and the bypass has m edges, so its cost is at most (m+4w+2)l<mh. The high and low edge sets have distinct rows/columns.
remaining_gap: Paths leaving the strip are outside the statement; no conclusion about unrestricted bigeodesics.

statement: For iid finite nonnegative nonconstant weights and thresholds l<h with p_l=P(t<=l)>0 and p_h=P(t>=h)>0, the slab trap of L1 has probability p_h^[m(2w+1)] p_l^[m+4w+2] >= exp(-C(w+1)^2), with m=floor((4w+2)l/(h-l))+1, K=1+4l/(h-l), C=2K log(1/p_h)+(K+4)log(1/p_l). Slabs spaced m+1 columns apart have independent events.
assumptions: fixed deterministic w, l, h and slab positions
proof_or_counterexample: The m(2w+1) high edges and m+4w+2 low edges are distinct. m<=K(w+1), 2w+1<=2(w+1), and m+4w+2<=(K+4)(w+1); since w+1<=(w+1)^2 the exponent bound follows. Consecutive supports at A and A+m+1 have disjoint horizontal edges and connector columns.
remaining_gap: The independence is for predetermined trap events only, never conditional on an adaptively selected path.

statement: For C from L2, deterministic nondecreasing integer w(n) with limsup w(n)/sqrt(log n)<1/sqrt(C), and fixed integer center y0, almost surely no injective ambient geodesic ray has a tail in |y-y0|<=w(|x|).
assumptions: iid finite nonnegative nonconstant weights on Z^2
geodesic ray means every finite subpath minimizes ambient passage time
proof_or_counterexample: At R=2^k let W=w(2R), m=m(W), and J=floor(R/(m+1)). J disjoint traps fit in [R,2R]. Choose theta with C limsup^2<theta<1; then q_W>=R^-theta and J>=cR/sqrt(log R), so exp(-Jq_W) is summable in k. On the resulting all-annuli event, any injective ray tail in the tube leaves every finite x-window, stays on one side, and crosses a trapped slab. Taking the last visit to its first column before the first arrival at the final column keeps the subpath within the slab, contradicting L1. Reflect for negative x.
remaining_gap: No confinement theorem places arbitrary bigeodesics in such tubes. This KEEP is a partial theorem only.

statement: Under T3's hypotheses, almost surely every injective ambient geodesic ray and every integer y0 satisfy limsup_j |y_j-y0|/sqrt(log(2+|x_j|))>=1/sqrt(C); thus no bigeodesic tail is eventually in a fixed finite-width horizontal or vertical strip.
proof_or_counterexample: For each rational 0<c<1/sqrt(C), w_c(n)=ceil(c sqrt(log(2+n))) meets T3. Intersect its probability-one events over countably many c and integer y0. A ray with smaller limsup eventually fits one of those tubes, contradiction. Rotate coordinates for vertical strips.
remaining_gap: The conclusion is axis-aligned and gives no unrestricted-bigeodesic exclusion.

statement: The accessible 2015 Auffinger-Damron-Hanson survey poses Question 31 as 'Do geodesic lines exist?' in section 4.5, printed page 86, zero-based PDF page 85; it does not state the explicit minimum-of-four moment condition found in the 2026 preprint.
source: https://sites.math.northwestern.edu/~auffing/FPPSurvey.pdf, PDF lines 4829-4832; w390/CLAIMS.jsonl source-6; intake brain_bundle_C006p01.json P0117
proof_or_counterexample: Direct source inspection locates the question and shows that the intake's PDF p.98 locator is version-dependent. The 2026 theorem's explicit moment assumption must be attributed to that preprint, not the bare survey question.
remaining_gap: The intake may refer to a different PDF edition; no claim about all versions' page numbers.

statement: If iid nonnegative Z^2 edge weights have P(t_e=0)>0, then almost surely there exists a noninjective doubly infinite nearest-neighbor sequence entirely in the row y=0 whose every finite segment has ambient minimum passage cost. Thus the injectivity condition in w390's tube theorem cannot be silently dropped for laws with zero atoms.
assumptions: walks with repeated vertices are allowed in the weakened assertion
source: owner-own-work; w392 boundary analysis of w390/PROOF.md Theorem 3
proof_or_counterexample: Along row y=0 the countably many horizontal edges are independent; the probability that none is zero is lim_N (1-p0)^N=0. Select a zero edge with endpoints u,v and let v_{2k}=u, v_{2k+1}=v for all k in Z. Every finite segment costs zero, and all passage times are nonnegative, so it minimizes. The sequence lies in a width-zero horizontal strip but repeats vertices.
remaining_gap: Counterexample concerns the weakened noninjective definition only; P0117's nonatomic target and w390's injective theorem are unaffected.

statement: For any stationary measurable finite nonnegative edge-weight field on nearest-neighbor Z^2, with A the vertices on simple bigeodesics, D_n the vertices of B_n lying on any simple globally minimizing path joining two vertices of boundary B_(2n), and H_n(v) a centered simple globally minimizing path with n edges in each arm, p=P(0 in A) satisfies p<=E|D_n|/|B_n|<=P(H_n(0)) decreasing to p. Thus absence of all bigeodesics almost surely is equivalent to E|D_n|=o(n^2).
assumptions: all simple geodesic witnesses included, ties allowed
source: w389/ATTEMPT.md C02 and drafts/bundle_001.json occupation-density; owner-own-work
proof_or_counterexample: Centered globally minimizing simple paths form a finitely branching tree under deletion of both end vertices. All H_m(v) hold iff an infinite branch gives a simple bigeodesic through v. For v in A∩B_n, first hits of boundary B_(2n) on its two arms witness v in D_n. For v in D_n, each endpoint has L-infinity distance at least n from v, so the two arms each have at least n edges and witness H_n(v). Take cardinalities, expectations, stationarity, then continuity from above. Countable union over all vertices converts p=0 to global absence.
remaining_gap: No iid bound E|D_n|=o(n^2) is obtained. This is a deterministic/stationary reduction only.

statement: If T_0 is the union of all infinite simple geodesic rays from 0 and q(x)=P(x in T_0), then for every n>=1, sum_{x in S_n}q(x)=E|T_0∩S_n|>=P(T_0 nonempty); if a ray exists almost surely, the sum is at least one and max_{x in S_n}q(x)>=1/(8n). Hence the proposed vanishing raw forward-ray shell sum and uniform o(1/n) rate are impossible.
assumptions: S_n is the L-infinity shell of size 8n
T_0 is all rays, not a selected ray tree
source: w389/ATTEMPT.md C03; w388/ATTEMPT.md corrected C03; owner-own-work
proof_or_counterexample: Each infinite ray starts inside B_(n-1) and leaves this finite box, so it hits S_n. Thus on {T_0 nonempty}, |T_0∩S_n|>=1; take expectation and use finite-sum linearity. The maximum is at least the average over 8n vertices. For iid atomless finite nonnegative weights, rays exist almost surely: choose c large so 4Eexp(-ct)<1, union-bound simple paths of length j with cost <=K, obtain finite geodesics to arbitrarily distant vertices, then extract an infinite geodesic prefix branch.
remaining_gap: The valid bigeodesic-to-shell incidence upper bound remains, but it cannot close P0117 through decay of this one-sided shell statistic. A genuinely two-sided estimate is missing.
